answer:
Recurring onboarding blockers across the playbook and implementation data are:

1. **Permission mapping / RBAC synchronization** – Aligning NovaLearn access controls with the customer’s Active Directory or folder permission structures. This accounts for 45% of onboarding delay incidents and is described as the most common blocker, with examples such as Acme Manufacturing and Meridian Retail Group experiencing AD sync issues [NL-031#NL-031-S04][NL-012#NL-012-S06][NL-005#NL-005-S06].

2. **Source ingestion cleanup** – Removing outdated, redundant, or corrupted files before indexing. Customers often upload un-reviewed folders, causing answers to draw from stale policies and pausing onboarding for manual document audits. This accounts for 30% of delays, with examples like Harbor Foods and Atlas Logistics [NL-031#NL-031-S04][NL-012#NL-012-S06][NL-005#NL-005-S02].

3. **OCR / scanned PDF processing** – Extracting readable text and formatting from image-only policy manuals. Standard parsing fails on image-only PDFs, producing empty indexes or incomplete citations and failing go-live citation thresholds. This accounts for 25% of delays; BrightPath Healthcare had the longest onboarding at 9.5 weeks due to scanned compliance files [NL-031#NL-031-S04][NL-012#NL-012-S06][NL-005#NL-005-S09][NL-005#NL-005-S02].

The playbook also codifies these as gate requirements and remediation triggers: stale document archiving in Phase 3, enterprise OCR queues, permission enforcement sign-off, and a mandatory corpus audit when UAT thresholds fail [NL-005#NL-005-S02][NL-005#NL-005-S09][NL-005#NL-005-S11].
